transcript: Josh Sharp's ta-da! is simply so gay and so chaotic, and so naturally, I loved it. It's an 80-minute solo show involving dozens of little personal anecdotes, one big takeaway, and 2,000 Powerpoint slides. That last part is really what intrigued me and got me to buy a ticket, and boy did it deliver on its promise. The whole show is quite a feat of precision, with Josh aligning the slides with the script in ways that are both creative and hilarious. For example, he often displays words or ideas that ironically juxtapose or add comedic subtext to what he's saying, adding a layer of comedy that only this form could bring. It also makes the whole experience very mentally stimulating for the audience, and I felt like the 80 minutes flew by. Perhaps most essentially, Josh has a lovely stage presence and delivers a lot of really funny material in the show. Like with the slides, there's a lot packed in here. It's about gayness and multiplicity and life and time, even Quantum Theory. All in all, would definitely recommend. ta-da! is running at the Greenwich House Theatre into mid-August. With that, another program for my collection.
